summary: This House resolution honors Dr. Jane Goodall after her death by formally recognizing her chimpanzee research and global conservation work, commending her education and youth programs, extending condolences to her family and institutes, and acknowledging her advocacy for ethical primate treatment.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a purely symbolic tribute with no provisions, authorizations, or implications related to federal spending levels or budgets.
No references to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures appear in the text.
The bill contains no content touching on healthcare systems, coverage, or policy.
No connection to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The resolution does not address immigration, borders, or related policies.
No mention of reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No bearing on military or defense spending or policy.

While the resolution honors Jane Goodall's environmental conservation work, it is strictly commemorative and enacts no policy changes, regulations, or funding decisions related to climate or environmental protections.
No provisions or implications regarding welfare programs or social safety net policies.
The text notes Goodall's educational efforts but does not alter federal education policy, funding, or structure.
No relation to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related issues.
The resolution has no connection to criminal justice reform or enforcement.
No engagement with trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No fiscal policy implications or references to deficits or debt.
The bill does not address LGBTQ+ rights or protections.
No provisions or discussion of foreign aid.
No relation to voting access, election integrity, or electoral policy.
The resolution contains no content on technology regulation or privacy.
No references to labor rights, unions, or employment policy.
The bill does not engage with religious liberty or anti-discrimination issues.
